title: A Method for the Construction of Minimum-Redundancy Codes (Huffman, 1952)
section: Derived Coding Requirements and the construction procedure
excerpt: The two least probable messages are combined into a single composite message whose probability is the sum of the two. This process is repeated, at each step combining the two least probable messages of the current ensemble, until only one message remains. Tracing back, each combination corresponds to a binary digit distinguishing the two combined messages. The average code length is the sum over messages of probability times code length, and no other code with the prefix property has a smaller average length.
focus: Explain Huffman's construction on 4-6 symbols with editable probabilities. Show the step-by-step merging of the two least probable nodes into a growing binary tree, the resulting codewords, each code length, and the average code length compared with a fixed-length code. Let the learner step through the merges and change the probabilities. Check that probabilities sum to 1, the code is prefix-free, and equal probabilities for 4 symbols give 2 bits each. Explain that Huffman is optimal only among symbol-by-symbol prefix codes.
audience: Engineering undergraduate who knows basic probability and binary numbers.
